subject: Dedicated sizing: baseline + burst decomposition for Helion Health
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helionhealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps <engops@helionhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing help — baseline vs burst, sample telemetry attached

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the routing/fallback ideas. We
need to firm up numbers for procurement: baseline sustained GPUs (for our day-to-day)
and burst headroom for peak clinical windows. Can you send the questionnaire you use
for pre-sales sizing?

Attached is a small sample of our telemetry (anonymized): short/long prompt mixes,
average response lengths, and a 72-hour token histogram. We want to avoid over-
committing but also need confidence that our 99th-percentile latency stays <250ms
for the interactive workflows.

Key asks:
- Recommend a minimal reserved footprint for our current traffic (approx. 1.2M tokens/day).
- Guidance on mapping prompt/response mixes to GPU SKU choices.
- What telemetry do you need to validate burst sizing?

Appreciate a short questionnaire or checklist we can fill; ideally a single spreadsheet.
Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up after you review the sample?

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Platform Integrations
Helion Health

[Attachment: helion_telemetry_sample.csv (text/csv, 180KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helionhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — baseline vs burst, sample telemetry attached

Jordan — thanks, received the telemetry sample and good notes. I pulled together a
focused pre-sales questionnaire that helps us translate token flow into a reserved
GPU footprint and burst window. I attached the workbook; main areas it covers:

1) Traffic profile (baseline RPS, peak-minute RPS, hourly distribution)
2) Prompt/response taxonomy (percent short/medium/long; examples)
3) Critical latency SLOs by route (interactive vs batch)
4) Session shape (KV-cache usage, multi-turn statefulness, average context length)
5) Failure/fallback tolerance (graceful degradation, lower-quality model fallback)
6) Telemetry samples we still need (per-route p50/p95/p99 token latencies, cold start samples)

Quick answers I can give from your sample:
- With 1.2M tokens/day concentrated mostly in daytime hours (~70%), a conservative
  starting reserved footprint is 2 x A10-equivalent GPUs for interactive routing (assumes
  Redwood continuous-batching and KV cache).
- For burst headroom targeting 10x baseline peak-minute RPS, plan for an additional
  6-8 transient GPUs depending on the model quantization.

That said, the workbook will let us finalize numbers. Can you review the attached
spreadsheet and populate the highlighted cells (baseline RPS, peak-minute, sample
prompt examples)? I recommend returning it before our follow-up so we can bring a
concrete sizing sketch.

Proposed times for a 30-min sync: Wed 08/26 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 08/27 15:00-15:30 PT —
I’ll send a calendar invite if one of those works.

Thanks — Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_questionnaire.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing help — baseline vs burst, sample telemetry attached

Mateo / Karthik — forwarding Jordan's telemetry and the questionnaire. Two quick
notes from pre-sales side:

- Pricing/commitment constraint: Helion prefers a small initial reserve with fast
  burst scaling rather than a large up-front commit. We should prepare a fallback
  plan that emphasizes GPU oversubscription and aggressive quantized variants for
  burst.
- For the follow-up call, let's have a short checklist: (1) confirm p95 targets by route,
  (2) model choice (Llama-70B float vs 8-bit quantized), (3) acceptable degradation
  path (e.g., stream shorter responses or allow 10% request rejection).

Karthik, can you precompute a couple of SKU-mapping scenarios (A10/RTX6000 vs
H100 light-quant) for 1x baseline, 4x peak, and 10x burst? Put numbers for estimated
GPU-hours/day and unit cost impact so we can show cost tradeoffs on the call.

Mateo — I’ll join the Wed/Thu slots if you book one.

— Marissa
Director, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helionhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — baseline vs burst, sample telemetry attached

Jordan — thanks for filling the workbook this morning (received v1). Quick summary
from our side and next steps:

Summary (high level):
- Baseline (sustained): 2 x A10-equivalent GPUs to meet daytime steady-state with
  KV cache hit assumptions you provided (65% hit). That maps to ~48 GPU-hours/day
  and meets p95 interactive target of ~120ms in our testing harness.
- Burst headroom: to cover the 10x peak-minute scenario with p95 latency <250ms,
  we recommend a transient pool of 6 H100-light quantized GPUs (or 8 A10s) for the
  15-minute window. That is sized conservatively; if you can accept aggressive
  model-variant fallback (shorter responses + 8-bit quant), we can shave 20-30%
  of burst cost.

Operational asks before commitment:
- Provide 48 hours of raw per-route p99 token-latency traces (we'll run a short stress
  replay).
- Confirm acceptable fallback (shorten responses OR fallback to quantized model).
- If you want dedicated tenancy, choose whether you prefer reserved capacity
  with burst bursting to shared pool, or fully pinned hardware (affects latency/cost).

Call: Wed 08/26 10:00 PT works for me; sending calendar invite now. Karthik will
bring SKU cost scenarios and Marissa will cover contract/commit options.

Attachments: I included an abridged sizing note (one-pager) in the workbook. After
our call we'll produce a brief 'footprint sketch' showing reserved GPUs, burst
allocation, and rough monthly cost at three commitment levels.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_questionnaire.xlsx (updated v1)]
